use_case_summary: Enterprise RAG for legal/compliance discovery. Primary workload: high-recall document search + evidence extraction. Pipeline: embed corpus -> approximate nearest neighbor retrieval -> cross-encoder rerank -> extractive answer generation. Concerned about per-query economics at 150 QPS peak and tail latency for top-5 accuracy.
notes:
- Customer: mid-size e-discovery & compliance services provider. heavy regulatory clients (financial services, pharma)
- Scale: target index ~150M documents (mixture of DIA, PDFs, PST extracts). Typical doc length varies; avg embedding token window requested ~2048 context.
- Performance targets: 95th percentile rerank+serve <250ms for SLA routes; prefer <150ms for internal analyst tier.
- Throughput: steady 60 QPS, peak 150 QPS during intake windows. P50 vs P95 latency split important.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming for <$0.05/query (embed+ann+rerank amortized). Wants clear unit economics: tokens, GPU seconds, storage.
- Model preferences: open embedding model acceptable (small/medium), but reranker must be cross-encoder (higher compute). Will consider quantized model variants; wants Redwood optimize recommendations.
- Routing/fallback: prefer primary private cluster (EU + NA regions) with automatic fallback to dedicated hosts if burst > capacity. Can tolerate degraded recall for non-critical routes.
- Security/compliance: strict audit logging (immutable), retention policy support (7 years, legal holds), SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, KMS integration, full security questionnaire answers required.
- Data residency: core corp and EMEA client data must remain in EU region; log aggregation permitted in NA only after DLP filtering.
- POC success metrics: recall@100 >= 0.82 on labeled set; top-3 rerank MRR improvement >15% vs baseline BM25; tail latency P95 <300ms for rerank path.
- Quote from Head of Search: "We need predictable economics and an audit trail we can hand to compliance — if that doesn't exist, it's a non-starter."
- Internal stakeholders: CTO, Head of Search (prod owner), Legal Ops, Security Architect. Procurement/finance loop may take 6-8 weeks after POC.
- Notes on integration: existing infra uses Postgres metadata store + S3 for raw docs. They want Redwood to integrate with existing S3 buckets via VPC peering and to provide connectors for incremental indexing.
- Risk items: immutable audit logs requirement may rule out hosted unless private offers equivalent guarantees; also worried about cold-start rerank GPUs cost during spikes.
- Non-functional asks: SLA for latency tiers, token-level cost breakdowns in console, per-route usage dashboards.
